question: What is the main job of the respiratory system?

options.B: Swapping oxygen and carbon dioxide in the body

explanation: The lungs take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide to keep body cells functioning. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is indoor smoke from firewood or charcoal harmful to the lungs?

options.A: It introduces tiny harmful particles into delicate lung tissues
options.B: It increases systemic blood pressure significantly
options.C: It depletes atmospheric oxygen inside homes
options.D: It instantly causes complete respiratory arrest

explanation: Burning cooking fuels poorly releases fine smoke particles that irritate and damage the airways over time. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which action is an example of primary prevention for lung disease?

options.A: Running rehab programs for chronic bronchitis patients
options.B: Performing routine chest X-rays on a coughing patient
options.C: Giving asthma medications during an attack
options.D: Encouraging a patient to stop smoking tobacco

explanation: Primary prevention stops an illness from starting by removing risk factors beforehand. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: A patient working in a dusty environment asks how to protect their lungs. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Increase heavy outdoor exercise every morning
options.B: Wear a protective mask when dust levels are high
options.C: Avoid drinking cold water during dry seasons
options.D: Take daily antibiotics to prevent lung infections

explanation: A mask acts as a physical barrier that stops dust from entering the breathing tubes. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which vaccine is given to newborns in Nigeria to protect against severe tuberculosis?
explanation: The BCG vaccine is given early in life as part of routine immunizations to prevent severe tuberculosis. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why do people need to take the flu vaccine every year?

options.A: The flu virus changes its genetic makeup frequently
options.B: Antibodies only target dead viral particles briefly
options.C: Manufacturing guidelines require yearly stock rotation
options.D: Immunity from the shot disappears after thirty days

explanation: Influenza viruses mutate rapidly, so the vaccine must be updated annually to match the new strains. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which workplace hazard is most common in mining and construction?
explanation: Mining and construction workers often breathe in crystalline silica dust, which can cause lung scarring. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main reason workers use water when cutting stones or concrete?

options.A: To keep the work area from becoming slippery
options.B: To cool down the cutting machine blades
options.C: To stop dust particles from flying into the air
options.D: To make the concrete blocks set faster

explanation: Water weighs down dust particles so they do not float into the air and get breathed in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?
explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early screening and treatment to stop a disease from getting worse. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: A patient has a cough lasting over three weeks. What is the first screening test usually done in Nigeria?

options.A: Skin allergy testing for food triggers
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
options.D: Sputum smear microscopy for TB bacteria

explanation: A long-lasting cough requires a sputum test to check for tuberculosis as a standard diagnostic step. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention for chronic illnesses?

options.A: Reducing complications and improving quality of life
options.B: Preventing initial exposure to harmful agents
options.D: Screening healthy populations for hidden diseases

explanation: Tertiary prevention helps manage long-term conditions to reduce disability and help patients live better. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) learns pursed-lip breathing. How does this help?

options.A: It keeps airways open longer to release trapped air
options.B: It cures inflammation in the lung alveoli
options.C: It blocks dust from entering the nose
options.D: It increases red blood cell production

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates gentle pressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing too quickly. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why is community health advocacy an important nursing duty?

options.A: It replaces the need for doctors in rural clinics
options.B: It guarantees that hospitals receive adequate funding
options.C: It addresses environmental and social factors affecting lung health
options.D: It eliminates all infectious diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses advocate for changes in policies and habits that tackle the root environmental causes of illness. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h7)

question: What is a key part of effective health education in local communities?

options.A: Using clear language that respects local cultural beliefs
options.C: Handing out free drugs without checking patients

explanation: Health communication must be simple and culturally appropriate so people can easily understand and apply it. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h7)
